## Tesla Software Updates Explained — How They Work in the UK
Source: https://teslaservice.co.uk/software-updates

Home / Guides / Software Updates
How over-the-air updates actually roll out, how to check your own version, and what to do when one stalls or something breaks.
Last fact-checked: 27 September 2026 . Release schedules, feature names and version numbering change frequently — for the live release feed, see Not a Tesla App in our resources list.
The basics

### How do Tesla updates actually get installed?
Every Tesla receives software updates over-the-air (OTA) through its built-in internet connection — no dealer or garage visit required, which is a genuine difference from almost every petrol car. When an update is ready, the touchscreen shows a notification; you can install immediately, schedule it (commonly overnight), or postpone it for a period.
Checking your version

### How do I check what version I'm running?
On the car: Controls > Software . This shows the current installed version and, if one is queued, the pending update and its size. The Tesla app mirrors this remotely, so you can check without being in the car.
Rollout timing

### Why does everyone else have an update before me?
Tesla stages rollouts rather than pushing to the entire fleet simultaneously — by region, hardware configuration (e.g. HW3 vs HW4 vehicles often get different timing or feature sets), and sometimes a smaller early group first specifically to catch problems before a wider release. Seeing other owners post about a new version days or weeks before it reaches you is normal, not a sign anything is wrong with your car.
When something goes wrong

### An update failed to install, or something broke afterwards — what now?
- Stalled or stuck install: a soft reboot usually clears it. Hold the two scroll wheels (or the equivalent steering control combination for your model) until the screen goes black and restarts. This does not erase your settings, profiles or data.
- A feature seems broken after updating: check Tesla's own release notes for that version first — some behaviour changes are intentional and documented, not bugs.
- Still broken after checking release notes: contact Tesla support directly. This is a software issue, not something an independent garage — however good — has any access to fix, since update servers and firmware are entirely controlled by Tesla.
Staying on an older version

### Can I just stay on my current version and skip updates?
You can defer an update for a period, but not indefinitely. Tesla eventually applies updates as mandatory, particularly ones addressing safety issues, so long-term version-skipping isn't something the car is designed to support.

## Tesla vs Rival EVs, Honestly
Source: https://teslaservice.co.uk/tesla-vs-rivals

Home / Guides / Tesla vs Rivals
An even-handed look at where Tesla genuinely leads, and where rivals have closed the gap or done better.
Last fact-checked: 28 September 2026 . General guidance — always check your own model's specifics and current official sources before relying on it for a decision.
Charging network

### Charging network: still a genuine Tesla advantage
Tesla's Supercharger network remains a genuine practical advantage in the UK — extensive coverage, generally high reliability, and increasingly open to non-Tesla EVs too (reducing this advantage's exclusivity over time, but not eliminating the benefit for Tesla owners of deep integration with the car's own navigation and trip planning).
Software & updates

### Software and over-the-air updates: a genuine Tesla strength, though the gap has narrowed
Tesla's approach to shipping meaningful new features and fixes via over-the-air software updates was a genuine differentiator for years, and remains a strength — but several rival manufacturers have significantly improved their own OTA update capability since, narrowing what was once a much larger gap.
Build quality & interior

### Build quality and interior fit-and-finish: a more mixed picture
This is genuinely more contested than either extreme suggests. Independent reviews and owner reports have historically noted more variability in panel gaps and interior fit-and-finish on some Tesla models, particularly earlier production years, compared with some established rivals with longer manufacturing experience — while other reviews rate specific Tesla models highly on this exact point. It's worth checking recent, model-specific reviews rather than relying on either brand's general reputation, since this varies meaningfully by specific model and production year.


## Towing with a Tesla in the UK
Source: https://teslaservice.co.uk/towing-caravans

Home / Guides / Towing & Caravans
What towing genuinely does to range, and practical guidance for UK caravan and trailer owners.
Last fact-checked: 28 September 2026 . General guidance — always check your own model's specifics and current official sources before relying on it for a decision.
Which models can tow

### Which Tesla models are actually rated to tow?
Towing capability and rated maximum towing weight vary significantly by model — some Tesla models are rated for meaningful towing with a factory or approved tow bar, while others aren't rated for towing at all. Always check your specific model and configuration's official rated towing capacity directly with Tesla rather than assuming based on the vehicle's size or a different model's specification.
The range impact

### How much does towing actually reduce range?
Significantly — towing adds substantial aerodynamic drag and weight, and UK owners commonly report range reductions in the region of 30-50% while actively towing a caravan or heavy trailer, compared with unladen range. This is a bigger effect than most owners expect coming from a petrol tow vehicle, where the fuel-consumption penalty while towing feels proportionally smaller against a larger energy reserve.
Practical guidance

### Planning a towing trip
Given the scale of the range impact:
- Plan charging stops assuming closer to half your normal range, not your unladen rated figure.
- Check your specific tow bar and electrics are Tesla-approved or explicitly compatible, not just physically fitting.
- Confirm your specific model's rated maximum towing weight and nose weight before assuming a caravan or trailer is suitable.
- Practice manoeuvring and reversing with the combination in a quiet, open area before a real trip if you're new to towing generally.


## Tesla Tyres, Brakes & Routine Maintenance
Source: https://teslaservice.co.uk/tyres-brakes-guide

Home / Guides / Tyres & Brakes
What genuinely wears differently on an EV, how regenerative braking changes brake maintenance, and what a Tesla actually needs versus a petrol car.
Last fact-checked: 28 September 2026 . General principles across Tesla's range — always check your own model's specific maintenance recommendations for exact intervals.
Tyre wear

### Why do Tesla tyres wear out faster?
Two compounding factors. Instant torque from an electric motor delivers power far more abruptly than a petrol engine's more gradual build-up, which puts more stress on the contact patch every time you accelerate. On top of that, a Tesla is typically heavier than an equivalent-sized petrol car because of the battery pack, and that extra weight accelerates tread wear on its own. The combination means many owners find they're replacing tyres somewhat more often than they were used to on a previous petrol car, particularly if driving style leans toward brisker acceleration.
Choosing tyres

### Do I need special EV tyres?
Not strictly — a Tesla will run on standard tyres of the correct size and rating. But many owners specifically choose EV-designed or reinforced tyres, which typically have a stiffer sidewall built to cope with the extra weight and torque, better rolling resistance for range, and in some cases acoustic foam bonded inside the tyre to cut down road noise — more noticeable in an EV without engine noise to mask it. If you're replacing tyres anyway, it's worth asking whichever garage does the job whether an EV-specific option is available for your size before defaulting to a standard equivalent.
Regenerative braking

### Does regen braking mean the brakes last longer?
Generally, yes, and often considerably so. Regenerative braking — using the electric motor to slow the car and recover energy back into the battery — handles most everyday deceleration, so the physical friction brakes do far less work than on a petrol car and typically last a lot longer before needing new pads or discs. The trade-off: brakes that are barely used can be more prone to corrosion or the callipers seizing slightly over time, particularly in wet or salted-road winter conditions, so they still benefit from periodic inspection and servicing even when the pads themselves have plenty of life left.
Brake fluid

### Do I still need to change the brake fluid?
Yes — this is one maintenance item that doesn't change with an EV. Brake fluid absorbs moisture from the surrounding air over time regardless of how much the brakes are physically used, which gradually lowers its boiling point and effectiveness in an emergency stop. Tesla's own guidance is to have the brake fluid checked, and replaced if needed, roughly every two years, independent of mileage or how lightly the brakes have been used.
The bigger picture

### What routine maintenance does a Tesla actually need?
- No engine oil, oil filter, spark plugs, timing belt or exhaust system — all eliminated compared with a petrol car.
- Tyre rotation and wear checks, more frequently than you might be used to (see above).
- Brake fluid check/replacement roughly every two years.
- Cabin air filter replacement periodically.
- Occasional coolant system check for the battery and motor cooling loop.
- Wiper blades and 12V auxiliary battery health, as with any car.
There's no fixed "service schedule" in the traditional sense, but an annual visual inspection at a competent garage — official or independent — is a sensible habit even without a mandated interval forcing it.


## Tesla Voice Commands Cheat Sheet — What Actually Works
Source: https://teslaservice.co.uk/voice-commands-cheatsheet

Home / Guides / Voice Commands
How to actually get good results from voice commands, and where it currently falls short.
Last fact-checked: 28 September 2026 . General guidance — always check your own model's specifics and current official sources before relying on it for a decision.
How it works

### How does Tesla's voice command system actually work?
Activated by a steering wheel button or a wake phrase depending on your car and software version, the system handles natural-language requests for common tasks — climate control, navigation, media, and various settings — processing much of it with genuine natural language understanding rather than requiring rigid exact phrases, which sets it apart from older, more limited in-car voice systems.
What it's good at

### Where it genuinely works well
Climate adjustments ('set the temperature to 20 degrees', 'turn on the seat heater'), navigation ('navigate to the nearest Supercharger'), and media control are all generally reliable and worth using regularly rather than reaching for the touchscreen while driving, which is both safer and often quicker.
Where it struggles

### Where it's less reliable
Highly specific or unusual settings changes, requests involving very uncommon place names, and commands issued in a noisy cabin (multiple people talking, loud music) are the areas most likely to need a repeat or a manual touchscreen fallback. If a command consistently fails, rephrasing more simply and directly usually works better than repeating the exact same phrasing louder.


## Tesla Warranty in the UK: What's Actually Covered (2026)
Source: https://teslaservice.co.uk/warranty-guide

Home / Guides / Warranty
What the published warranty terms actually cover, and how to check your own car's specific status.
Last fact-checked: 28 September 2026 . General guidance — always check your own model's specifics and current official sources before relying on it for a decision.
The two main warranties

### What are the separate warranty categories?
Tesla typically publishes two headline warranties: a new-vehicle limited warranty covering general manufacturing defects for a set period/mileage, and a separate, usually longer, battery and drive unit warranty specifically covering the traction battery pack and motor(s), including excessive capacity degradation below a stated threshold — not just outright failure. Terms and exact mileage/year limits vary by model and have changed over different production periods, so always check your specific car's terms using its VIN rather than a generic figure.
What's excluded

### What typically isn't covered
Standard exclusions across most manufacturer warranties apply: wear-and-tear items (tyres, wiper blades, brake pads under normal wear), damage from accidents or misuse, and — as with any warranty — work carried out incorrectly by a third party can affect a claim for the specific system affected, though routine maintenance at a competent independent garage does not generally void the wider warranty under UK consumer law.
Checking your own car

### How to check your specific car's current warranty status
The only reliable way to know your exact terms and remaining cover:
- Check your warranty status and terms directly through your Tesla Account or app, which shows your specific car's VIN-linked coverage.
- For a used purchase, ask the seller for the original warranty start date and any transferred terms, and verify independently with Tesla rather than relying solely on the seller's description.
- Keep every service and repair invoice regardless of which garage did the work — this documentation matters if a warranty question ever arises.


## Which Tesla Should I Buy? A Quick Quiz for UK Buyers
Source: https://teslaservice.co.uk/which-tesla-quiz

Home / Guides / Which Tesla Quiz
A few honest questions to point you toward the right model for your actual situation, not just the newest one.
Last fact-checked: 28 September 2026 . General guidance — always check your own model's specifics and current official sources before relying on it for a decision.
Budget first

### Start with a realistic budget, including running costs
Before comparing models, work out a realistic total budget including insurance (see our insurance guide, since this varies more by model than many buyers expect), home charging setup if needed, and — if buying new — how UK price changes over a model's life might affect resale timing. A model that's a stretch to buy but comfortable to run beats one that's affordable to buy but strains your budget on insurance and running costs.
Use case

### Match the model to what you'll actually use it for
Daily commuting with occasional long trips suits a different model and battery size than genuine everyday long-distance driving. If you regularly carry more than two passengers, need to tow (see our towing guide), or want third-row seating, that narrows the field considerably before styling or performance preferences even come into it. Be honest about your actual typical use rather than the occasional edge case you might use to justify a bigger, more expensive model.
New vs used

### New, used, or wait for the next update?
See our dedicated new vs used vs wait page for the fuller trade-off, but as a starting principle: a used model from a well-established production run often offers better value than the newest available variant, unless a specific new feature genuinely matters to your use case rather than just being new.


## Tesla Windscreen Replacement & Camera Calibration Guide (UK)
Source: https://teslaservice.co.uk/windscreen-camera-calibration

Home / Guides / Windscreen Calibration
Why this is more involved — and more important — than replacing glass on an older car.
Last fact-checked: 28 September 2026 . General guidance — always check your own model's specifics and current official sources before relying on it for a decision.
Why it matters

### Why does a windscreen replacement need calibration at all?
Tesla's driver-assistance and Autopilot features rely on cameras mounted behind the windscreen, precisely aligned to interpret the road correctly. Replacing the glass — even with a correct OEM-spec part — can shift that alignment by a fraction of a degree, which is enough to affect how accurately the car reads lane markings, other vehicles and pedestrians. Recalibration resets that alignment; skipping it risks degraded or inconsistent driver-assistance performance without any obvious visual sign that something's wrong.
What's involved

### What does calibration actually involve?
Typically a combination of a static calibration (using specific targets positioned at exact distances in a controlled space) and a dynamic calibration (a supervised drive under specific conditions letting the car's software confirm the cameras are reading correctly). Not every independent garage has this equipment or the specific procedure — this is one area worth explicitly asking about before booking.
What to check

### What to check before and after the job
Before booking, and after collection:
- Ask specifically whether the garage performs camera calibration in-house or subcontracts it — either can be fine, but you should know which.
- Confirm the glass being fitted is the correct specification for a car with driver-assistance cameras, not a generic aftermarket windscreen.
- After collection, test Autopilot or lane-assist features in a safe, familiar area before relying on them for a longer trip.
- Keep the calibration certificate or confirmation, particularly relevant if you sell the car later.


## Tesla Winter Survival Guide (UK)
Source: https://teslaservice.co.uk/winter-survival-guide

Home / Guides / Winter Survival
Getting through a proper UK winter without any of the classic frozen-Tesla frustrations.
Last fact-checked: 28 September 2026 . General guidance — always check your own model's specifics and current official sources before relying on it for a decision.
Frozen handles

### Dealing with frozen door handles
Retractable door handles can occasionally freeze in place during a hard frost or after freezing rain. Most models have a manual override or a firmer push/pull technique documented in the owner's manual for exactly this situation — familiarise yourself with it before you actually need it in a hurry. Parking with handles less exposed to direct freezing rain where possible, and running a scheduled preconditioning session before you need to leave, both reduce how often this happens.
Preconditioning

### Using preconditioning properly
Scheduling departure time with preconditioning enabled warms the cabin and battery while the car is still plugged in, using mains power rather than your driving range — genuinely one of the most useful winter features available, and worth setting up as a routine for a regular commute rather than only using it occasionally.
Ice, snow & range

### Driving on ice/snow and planning for reduced range
Standard winter driving caution applies regardless of powertrain — reduced speed, increased following distance, and winter tyres if you regularly drive in genuinely snowy or icy conditions, since a Tesla's instant torque can make wheelspin easier to trigger on a slippery surface if not driven with appropriate care. Combine this with the range planning covered in our range by season page, since winter range reduction and slippery-condition driving often occur together.
